heading: Training & Workshops
intro: Beginner workshop proposals for educational partners in Agadir. Explore practical AI security ideas through simple explanations, synthetic examples and small guided activities.
format: Proposed in-person sessions in Agadir or remote sessions, subject to agreement with a host.
availability: No sessions are scheduled. Dates, language, fees, group size and delivery readiness need to be agreed with the host.
approach: Begin with a plain-English explanation and a realistic use case.
Use a fictional support assistant and synthetic data for demonstrations.
Give learners one small activity before reviewing their reasoning.
End with a short checklist and the limits of what the activity demonstrates.
deliveryNote: These are proposed introductory sessions, not delivered courses or a certification program. A host should review the syllabus, sample material and facilitator readiness before confirming a session.

contact.heading: Discuss an educational partnership
contact.intro: Use the existing GitHub profile to review Ahmed’s public work and any contact options he has chosen to make available there.
contact.limitation: This website has no configured email address or message form. The GitHub link opens a public profile; it does not send a message or reserve a workshop, and a private contact option may not be available.
checklist: Training center or group name, and the learner audience
Workshop title, preferred language and prior knowledge
Suggested dates, format, group size and available equipment
Host review, accessibility needs and a reliable contact method

workshops.title: AI security foundations: data, identity and boundaries
workshops.audience: Students and junior developers curious about AI application security.
workshops.summary: Follow a fictional customer-support assistant from a user request to private data and an action proposal.
prerequisites: Basic web browsing; no programming required.
outcomes: Identify the user, data owner and action service in a small AI workflow.
Distinguish authentication from permission to access a particular record.
Explain one place where a data or action permission must be checked.

agenda.title: Use case and vocabulary
agenda.activity: Introduce a fictional support assistant, users, private tickets and tools.

agenda.title: Identity, ownership and actions
agenda.activity: Trace who requests information and who can authorize an effect.

agenda.title: Guided boundary-mapping activity
agenda.activity: Learners annotate a synthetic workflow with identities and permission checks.

agenda.title: Review and take-away checklist
agenda.activity: Discuss the maps, unanswered questions and what would require a real security test.

workshops.takeaway: A learner-annotated workflow and a list of questions for a future security review.
workshops.scope: A conceptual introduction using fictional data. It does not assess a live product or establish security competence.

workshops.title: Safer AI use for students and educators
workshops.audience: Students, educators and staff beginning to use AI assistants.
workshops.summary: Practise handling sensitive information, checking sources and deciding when human review is needed.
prerequisites: Basic web browsing; no AI account or paid subscription required.
outcomes: Identify sensitive information in a fictional document before sharing it with an AI tool.
Separate a supported answer from a claim that still needs verification.
Describe when a proposed action needs a person’s review.

agenda.title: Everyday AI use cases
agenda.activity: Introduce fictional classroom and administrative scenarios.

agenda.title: Privacy and source checks
agenda.activity: Review synthetic documents and sample AI answers without submitting real personal data.

agenda.title: Small-group review activity
agenda.activity: Learners decide what to remove, verify or escalate in a fictional example.

agenda.title: Discussion and personal checklist
agenda.activity: Review decisions and prepare a short checklist for future AI use.

workshops.takeaway: A short checklist for data sharing, source verification and human review.
workshops.scope: An introductory practice session; institutional data policies and tool settings still need separate review.

workshops.title: Prompt injection awareness with a controlled demo
workshops.audience: Junior developers and technical students familiar with basic AI assistants.
workshops.summary: Inspect a prepared example where a retrieved document tries to influence an assistant’s behavior.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with AI assistants or the W01 introduction.
A browser for an optional local demonstration; printed transcripts are an alternative.
outcomes: Recognize an instruction attempt inside untrusted source material.
Distinguish a model’s proposed action from permission to execute it.
Describe a test and the evidence needed to evaluate a protective control.

agenda.title: Instructions and untrusted content
agenda.activity: Introduce the fictional retrieval workflow and the demonstration’s scope.

agenda.title: Facilitator-led synthetic demo
agenda.activity: Compare prepared transcripts; an optional local mock needs no paid API or external target.

agenda.title: Learner analysis
agenda.activity: Learners identify the attempted boundary crossing and propose a permission check and test.

agenda.title: Evidence and limitations
agenda.activity: Review observations and distinguish a mock result from evidence about an actual model or production system.

workshops.takeaway: An annotated transcript, a proposed control and one test idea.
workshops.scope: Only synthetic transcripts or a local mock. No testing of public services; no claim of a universal prompt-injection solution.

workshops.title: Linux permissions and evidence for AI application labs
workshops.audience: Technical beginners preparing for small AI application security labs.
workshops.summary: Inspect a disposable sample workspace and explain file ownership, permissions and command evidence.
prerequisites: A browser and access to Google Cloud Shell or a local Linux terminal.
Cloud Shell sign-in and availability should be checked by the host before scheduling; a transcript alternative can be used.
outcomes: Distinguish a regular file from a directory in a sample workspace.
Interpret owner, group and other permission bits without claiming they explain every access-control rule.
Record an inspection command’s output and its own exit status.

agenda.title: Workspace and evidence basics
agenda.activity: Introduce the disposable sample directory and explain command scope.

agenda.title: Reading file metadata
agenda.activity: Demonstrate type, owner, group and symbolic and numeric permissions.

agenda.title: Learner inspection activity
agenda.activity: Learners inspect sample entries and record their own command results.

agenda.title: Review and transfer
agenda.activity: Discuss evidence limits and why file access matters for an AI application’s data and credentials.

materials: A prepared terminal transcript as a fallback
workshops.takeaway: A small inspection record with the learner’s explanation and command exit statuses.
workshops.scope: Read-only inspection of sample files. No production data, credentials or permission changes are needed.
